 Jennifer Lawrence reveals the cringey comment she made after kissing ‘Silver Linings Playbook’ co-star Bradley Cooper 
 By 
 Eric Todisco 
 Published 
 Oct. 28, 2026, 10:39 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Jennifer Lawrence revealed she had an awkward interaction with Bradley Cooper when they filmed their “big makeout session” at the end of “Silver Linings Playbook.”
 “I said, ‘Aren’t you so sick of kissing?’ And he didn’t like that,'” Lawrence, 36, recalled on Alex Cooper’s “Call Her Daddy” podcast on Wednesday.
 “But I think he laughed,” she added of Bradley, 51.

 Lawrence said the exchange “was one of those moments where you’re like, ‘Right?’ And the other person’s like, ‘Oh.'”
 Regardless, Lawrence shared that the interaction was one of her favorite memories from making her 2012 Oscar-winning film, in which she played a young widow who falls for a recent divorcée with bipolar disorder (played by Bradley).
 Lawrence admitted on the podcast that she “was definitely nervous” meeting Bradley for the first time.
 “He was in ‘The Hangover.’ He was the biggest celebrity I think I ever met at that time,” she noted. “And I was like, ‘Watch this. Hold my beer.'”
 8 
 But Lawrence clarified that Cooper “laughed” at her comment afterwards. ©Weinstein Company/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 8 
 Lawrence also admitted she was “nervous” to meet Cooper on the set of the film. ©Weinstein Company/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 For the David O’Russell-directed film, Lawrence said that while she pretended to be “confident” in her dance skills, she really thought her moves were “so bad.”
 “After we finished filming, I had to do ADR to say like, ‘Yeah, I’m not that good of a dancer, but I like it, It’s fun, it makes me happy,’ because my dancing was so bad and it needed to be explained in the movie,'” she shared.
 Lawrence added that “if you put a gun to my head while we were shooting, I would’ve been like, ‘I’m really, really good. I’m an amazing dancer.'”

 “He was in ‘The Hangover.’ He was the biggest celebrity I think I ever met at that time,” Lawrence recalled. (Cooper and Lawerence are seen here in the film.) ©Weinstein Company/Courtesy Everett Collection

 Elsewhere on the podcast, Lawerence revealed she didn’t think the film — which grossed over $236 million worldwide and earned eight Oscar noms — would be so successful.
 “You never really do — unless you’re making ‘The Hunger Games’ or whatever,'” she said. “But no. “
 Lawrence then joked, “And I felt like the whole time like I don’t get it. Like, what is this movie about?”
 From working together on “Silver Linings Playbook,” Lawrence and Bradley created a close bond and reunited on screen for 2013’s “American Hustle,” 2014’s “Serena” and 2015’s “Joy.”
 8 
 Lawrence (seen here with Cooper in 2015) said that “if you put a gun to my head while we were shooting, I would’ve been like, ‘I’m really, really good. I’m an amazing dancer.'” Getty Images 
 8 
 Lawrence and Cooper (seen here in 2013) have worked together on four films and are close friends. Charley Gallay 
 Lawrence, during a 2015 red carpet Q&A , said, “I forced him to come onto [‘Serena’]. I mean, any male role is going to make me think of Bradley because in my opinion, he’s the best, and I love working with him.” 
 Bradley chimed in that he respects Lawrence “so much as a professional, as an actor, and I think she’s the best there is.”
 “And I just learn from her,” he added. “You always want to work with people that are better than you.”
